subject: Phased evaluation and commit schedule for AWS Private Offer
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acme.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Phased evaluation and commit schedule for AWS Private Offer

Jordan — thanks again for the time today. As discussed, attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that aligns the proof-of-value (PoV) evaluation with a staged private-offer commercial path on AWS. High-level summary below, then the MAP attachment (ACME-MAP-v1.0.xlsx) has the weekly milestones and success criteria.

Quick summary: 
- Week 0–2: PoV setup (sample data ingest, network allowlist, baseline latency/cost metrics) — Redwood provides dedicated sandbox cluster.
- Week 3–4: Feature validation (multi-turn replies, domain-specific prompt tuning).
- Week 5: Midpoint review — if success criteria met, ACME agrees to a 3-month pilot commit (reserved capacity equivalent) to run pilot workloads.
- Pilot (month 1–3): Ramp to target throughput; pricing move from evaluation rate -> pilot committed rate with 10% discount applied to token/unit price.
- Post-pilot (month 4): Option to convert to 12-month private offer with stepped discounts at 6- and 12-month commit thresholds.

Ask: Can you confirm the technical success criteria in the attached worksheet and confirm that procurement will engage for a private offer once we pass the Week 5 checkpoint? If helpful, I can loop in our Marketplace team to prepare the AWS private offer draft so procurement can review.

Attachments: ACME-MAP-v1.0.xlsx (MAP workbook)

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0148

From: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acme.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>, ACME Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Phased evaluation and commit schedule for AWS Private Offer

Neha — appreciate the clear plan. A couple notes from our side:

1) Timeline constraint: our Q3 board review closes July 20; we need a commercial trigger before July 15 to include any material in the Q3 commit ask. That means the Week 5 checkpoint needs to align no later than July 10.
2) Commercial ask: procurement prefers a staged private offer with explicit commit/discount tiers (e.g., 0–3 months pilot at list-10%, 3–6 months at list-15% if committed, 6–12 months at list-20%). We need the exact pricing bands and billing entity (ACME Global or ACME US).
3) Security/compliance: our InfoSec team will request SOC2 artifacts and a short architecture diagram showing data flow for the sandbox.

Can you provide a redline of proposed private-offer terms and confirm whether AWS private offers can be issued with an initial 90-day pilot commitment that transitions into a 12‑month locked price? If not, what are the alternatives?

Jordan Ellis
Head of Platform Engineering, ACME Corp
jordan.ellis@acme.com | +1 212-555-1010

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acme.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Phased evaluation and commit schedule for AWS Private Offer

Jordan — great notes. Quick answers and next steps below.

- Q3 timing: we can accelerate the sandbox onboarding to start Week 0 on Monday June 29 so the Week 5 checkpoint falls around July 6–8. That meets your July 10 milestone.
- Pricing bands: Draft proposal attached; high-level sample: evaluation (pay-as-you-go) -> pilot (3-month commit) = 10% off list; 6-month commit = 15% off; 12-month commit = 20% off. We will model these as billing credits applied in the private offer so pricing is explicit in the offer.
- Private offer mechanics on AWS: AWS supports staged/private offers; we can issue an initial 90-day private offer that includes a conversion pathway to a 12-month agreement. The private-offer draft will include the staged commit schedule and a DocuSign link for the commercial signature post-acceptance.
- Security: attaching our standard SOC2 evidence bundle link and a short architecture diagram; we'll also provide a sandbox VPC diagram for the PoV.

Next actions: Karthik/Marissa — can you create the private-offer draft and the pricing ladder (PDF) for Jordan's procurement team? I'll coordinate the MAP workbook updates and push the Week 0 kick-off calendar invite after we get procurement contact.

Attachments: Redwood-PrivateOffer-Terms-20260630.pdf (draft pricing ladder and private-offer language)

Thanks,
Neha

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Phased evaluation and commit schedule for AWS Private Offer

Neha / Marissa — copying a few quick negotiation points to keep the MAP commercially executable and protect economics: 

- Tie the 10% pilot discount to a minimum usage commit (we recommend reserved GPU-hours equivalent to $18k/month) to avoid open-ended pilot consumption.
- Include a mutual success clause at Week 5 with defined metrics (latency < 250ms P95, accuracy uplift on labeled set >= 12%, error rate < 1.5%). If metrics not met, automatic 30-day extension (no penalty) rather than immediate commit.
- For the AWS private offer, model discounts as percentage off list with a step-change rebate applied as an invoice credit after conversion — this avoids changing SKU pricing mid-pilot and keeps AWS merchant-of-record flow intact.
- Provide an escape hatch for capacity (burst policy) for the pilot month 2 if production load spikes — helps ACME avoid throttling.

I'll attach the term PDF (Redwood-PrivateOffer-Terms-20260630.pdf) with the commit thresholds and suggested billing entity language. Marissa, happy for you to push to procurement and include the HubSpot deal link for tracking.

Karthik
Commercial Lead | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acme.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>, ACME Procurement <procurement@acme.com>

Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Private offer and MAP update (next steps)

Jordan / Priya / Procurement — attaching an updated MAP workbook (sheet: commercial-summary) and the private-offer draft. Next steps to keep us on track for ACME's July board window: 

1) Procurement: please confirm the billing entity (ACME Global vs ACME US) and whether you require a PO for the 90-day pilot. If a PO is required we can issue a preliminary invoice schedule to match.
2) Legal/commercial: we'll send the private-offer DocuSign for signature once procurement confirms billing details and we clear any minimal legal redlines.
3) Tech: Neha will kick off sandbox provisioning on June 29. Please expect a calendar invite from her with VPC allowlist details.

Links: HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/98765 | DocuSign preview: https://www.docusign.com/1234-priv-offer-acme

Attachments: ACME-MAP-v1.0.xlsx, Redwood-PrivateOffer-Terms-20260630.pdf

Thanks — can procurement reply with billing entity and PO cadence today if possible? That will let us finalize the private offer and keep the Week 5 checkpoint in time for your July board queue.

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0199

Marissa / Team — procurement confirmed: billing entity = ACME US. Procurement can issue a PO covering the 90-day pilot; legal will review the DocuSign private-offer language and come back with any redlines by June 3 (typo in original thread? should be July 3). We accept the staged discount ladder as described (pilot: 10% / 6-month: 15% / 12-month: 20%) pending the Week 5 success metrics.

Jordan and I are aligned to proceed — please send the DocuSign and sandbox invite; procurement will upload the PO once DocuSign is accepted.

Thanks,
Priya Shah
